title: Diagnose a pipeline failure
summary: Find the first supported cause, then choose a useful next action.

sections.label: Inputs
sections.text: The failed run and candidate revision, the stage that failed, relevant logs or reports, expected behavior and any known environment changes.

sections.label: Procedure
items: Identify the first actionable failure. Later errors may be consequences.
Compare the observation with the expected behavior and identify the affected part of the work.
Separate possible implementation, fixture, dependency, access and infrastructure causes. Keep uncertain causes explicit.
Inspect evidence for the strongest explanation. Use an approved read path for logs and reports.
Choose a bounded next action. If a correction is made, rerun the affected checks for the corrected candidate and retain the actual result.

sections.label: Output
sections.text: A finding with the run and revision, the observed failure, supporting evidence, remaining uncertainty, checks actually performed and the proposed next action.

sections.label: Acceptance checks
sections.text: Another reviewer can find the relevant evidence and distinguish a proposed explanation from a verified correction. Stop repeated retries when they add no new evidence.

sections.label: Choose the relevant environment
sections.text: Jenkins diagnosis is one specialist example. Use the same evidence questions with another pipeline system, then supply that system's actual run identifiers, access path and commands. Atlas does not invent or connect those interfaces.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
sections.text: Capture a failing run during reproduction, test possible causes during diagnosis and rerun the affected checks for the repaired candidate during regression. The workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Only the source contribution below was verified on 15 October 2026, not every original assertion or project outcome.

sections.label: Gap review: acceptance outputs
items: A failure record preserves run identity, candidate revision, first actionable error and source locations.
A hypothesis record states what observation would support or reject each plausible cause and names the bounded next action.
A correction record compares expected and observed rerun results for the changed candidate, retaining untested assumptions.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: Jenkins documents selecting an individual Pipeline run and viewing its full Console Output. This is one concrete pipeline evidence access example. Other systems need their actual supported interfaces. The source does not validate an inferred cause or a repair. Review date: 15 October 2026. This review covers this source contribution only, not the whole guide.

confidence: Moderate. Validate the procedure in your environment

catalog.applicability: Use when an automated pipeline fails and a team needs an evidence based diagnosis. A pipeline system or AI agent is not prescribed.
catalog.limits: This is a proposed reading procedure. It does not select an exportable skill, configure access, run checks or establish a successful result.
